Title:  Regarding establishment o Passport Seva Kendra at Punalur. 

SHRI N. K. PREMACHANDRAN (KOLLAM): Thank you, Mr. Chairman, Sir. My ‘Zero Hour’ submission is in respect of one of the important demands of my constituency, Kollam in Kerala. Punalur town is a municipal town on the eastern part of Kollam district and it belongs to my constituency. There are numerous people who are employed outside in foreign countries and a lot of people are going abroad for employment, study and even for visit. But it is quite unfortunate to note that there is no Passport Seva Kendra in Punalur area. Though it is densely populated and a large number of people are working abroad, but there is no Passport Seva Kendra. The nearest Passport Seva Kendra is in Kollam town and the next one is at Thiruvananthapuram. As far as the people of Punalur are concerned, it is very difficult for them to go to Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam to get the passport facilities. 

So, my humble submission, through you, to the Government, especially to the External Affairs Minister is to commence a Passport Seva Kendra on the eastern part of Kollam district, that is at Punalur. That is one of the necessities of the district. I once again urge upon the Minister of External Affairs to give sanction for commencing a Passport Seva Kendra at Punalur. 

Thank you very much, Sir.

Title:  Regarding hike in petroleum prices. 

DR. DNV SENTHILKUMAR S. (DHARMAPURI): Vanakkam Chairperson, Sir. This is regarding the recent hike in petrol price, diesel price and price of LPG cylinders. This affects the common man. What is the Government going to do to regulate the continuous increase of the fuel price? 

We have seen that often the Government comes out saying that they do not have anything to regulate the prices. They say that it is the oil companies which regulate the prices. 

But during elections, the prices freeze magically. There is no price rise during that time in spite of the oil price going above 100 dollar a barrel. There will be no fluctuation in prices. Recently, we have seen, despite start of the Russia-Ukraine conflict there has not been any increase in the prices of petrol and diesel as it was the election time here.

So, I sincerely urge upon the Government, through the Chairperson, to direct the Election Commission to keep on conducting elections throughout the year, because that is the only way by which the common man can be saved from the price hike of petrol and diesel. Or, we will be in a state of fear that the price of petrol, diesel and LPG may fluctuate from morning to evening. There may be one price in the morning and another in the evening. So, to save the common man, I urge upon this Government to come up with a proposal to have elections throughout the year.

Thank you, Sir.

Title:  Regarding shortage of teachers in Kendriya Vidyalaya in Kalburgi. 

DR. UMESH G. JADAV (GULBARGA): I would like to raise a very important issue pertaining to the shortage of teachers in Kalaburagi Kendriya Vidyalaya in the State of Karnataka.

Sir, the vacancy in the post of teachers is having a negative impact on the educational system. This in turn creates instability among parents who have enrolled their children in these schools.

It is estimated that around 50-60 per cent of the teachers’ posts in 50 Central Schools, in the State of Karnataka itself, are lying vacant and these Kendriya Vidyalayas are running their classes with guest faculties. With the guest faculties, we cannot expect quality education which was being imparted by the permanent faculties as tough procedures are followed while recruiting the permanent faculty. Sir, I would like to take the example of Kalaburagi Kendriya Vidyalaya itself, where there are 12 sanctioned posts of teachers in Primary Section, out of which only five posts are filled, and the rest seven posts are vacant. In Higher Secondary section, out of 15 sanctioned posts only four are filled and 11 posts are vacant. The reason behind this vacancy is, the Government has relaxed its transfer policy. Teachers from North India are being recruited in the schools of Karnataka. After relaxation of the transfer policy, they have taken transfer to north, and this is creating a lot of problems.

Kalaburagi is the most backward area. We had also requested for one more Kendriya Vidyalaya in the north part of Kalaburagi.

Title:  Regarding EPF 95 -pension. 

श्री सी.पी. जोशी (चित्तौड़गढ़): महोदय, आपने मुझे शून्यकाल में बोलने का मौका दिया, इसके लिए आपका धन्यवाद  । 

महोदय, मैं आपका ध्यान उन लोगों की तरफ आकृष्ट करना चाहता हूँ, जो पेंशनर हैं  । ईपीएस पेंशनर-95 की सूची में बहुत लंबित माँगें उन लोगों की देश भर में चल रही हैं  । देश भर में लगभग 65-70 लाख लोग हैं और मेरी कांस्टिट्यूएंसी में लगभग 30 से 40 हजार लोग ऐसे हैं, जो आज भी इस माँग के पूरा होने की बाट जोह रहे हैं  ।

Title:  Regarding Construction of bridges accross Vedavathi (Hagari) river. 

DR. SANJEEV KUMAR SINGARI (KURNOOL): Thank you, hon. Chairperson, Sir. I am raising a matter with regard to a bridge connecting Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. For more than a decade, the people of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka have been requesting for the construction of a bridge across Vedavathi river, which is also called Hagari river. The river divides Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka, which forms the boundary line for nearly twenty kilometres. A bridge connecting Gulyam village of Andhra Pradesh and Basarkod village of Karnataka will benefit lakhs of people of Bellary district and Halaharvi Mandal of Andhra Pradesh. A few years back, during his visit to the Bellary district, the hon. Minister of Road Transport and Highways had promised to sanction a bridge here.  Hon. Chairperson, Sir, there are four points of justification for the request of a bridge. Firstly, Gulyam village of Andhra Pradesh is famous for 200 years old Gadilingeswara Temple. Daily, hundreds of people from Karnataka traverse the riverbed and visit the temple. Likewise, thousands of devotees visit the temple every new moon day and lakhs of people visit the temple annually on the car festival day. Similarly, Chellaguriki village of Bellary district has famous Sri Yerrithatha Swamy temple, which attracts thousands of devotees from Andhra Pradesh. The proposed bridge facilitates pilgrims from Andhra Pradesh. 

There is an alternate route which is 27 kilometres long. The journey is very tedious. It is an arduous journey. So, majority of the commuters prefer to cross the river bed and this bridge reduces nearly 27 kilometres of that hard journey. 

There is a lot of human loss and property loss during flash floods. So, I request the hon. Minister to consider this promise. People of both States have social networking since ages. The proposed bridge can strengthen inter-State social networking for health, education, business and marriages. Sir, there is a famous quote. ‘American roads are not good because America is rich but America is rich because American roads are good. The same quotation is seen on the walls of office of the hon. Minister of Road, Transport and Highways. 

I request the Government of India to make their slogan worthwhile – Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Viswas and Sabka Prayas. So, this is a promise given by hon. Minister. I request the Minister to keep his promise. Thank you, Sir.

Title:  Regarding the increase in prices of medicines. 

SHRI M. K. RAGHAVAN (KOZHIKODE): The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority of India on 25th March, 2022 has announced a 10.7 percent change in the Wholesale Price Index for the calendar year 2021 over the corresponding period in 2020. This would mean that nearly 800 scheduled medicines included in the National List of Essential Medicines, used in most common ailments, will now increase by a steep 10.7 percent beginning 1st April, 2022. This list will include medicines such as paracetamol, Azithromycin, other antibiotics, other mineral and vitamin tablets etc. These medicines are used to treat common conditions such as fever, infections, heart diseases, hypertension, skin diseases and anaemia, among others. If such a hike is effected, it can significantly affect a large number of Indians. Such a price increase will lead to disruption of our pharma chains and will only help the private companies in amassing huge profits. This situation is quite unwarranted in a country like India where lifestyle diseases and neglected tropical diseases are on the rise. A significant number of our people depends upon these essential medicines to save lives. I request the Government to urgently intervene and do the needful so that this draconian measure is not implemented. Thank you, Sir.

Title:  Regarding return of MBBS students from Ukraine and waiving of student loan. 

SHRI ANTO ANTONY (PATHANAMTHITTA): Thank you, Chairman. 

Chairman Sir, I invite the attention of this august House and the Government to the plight of the MBBS students returned to India from Ukraine. Their future is under the shadow of uncertainty as they could not complete the course. More than 25000 Indian students, ranging from the first year to the final year, pursue their MBBS Degree in Ukraine. They have already spent several lakhs of rupees as a course fee. These students are very much worried about their future. The Government may take up the issue with the officers concerned and find out a solution to help the students. If it is difficult to continue studying in Ukraine, the National Medical Commission may come up with a solution to help these students so that they can successfully complete their courses. I also request the Government to kindly waive off the educational loans taken by the students, who are doing courses in Ukraine. As this August House is aware of more than 25000 Indian students have enrolled in various medical colleges and universities in Ukraine, out of this, more than 5000 students are from Kerala. These students joined the course with the help of educational loans from various nationalised banks in our country. However, the future of these students is under question now. Therefore, I request the Government to kindly waive off their loan amount and also provide an alternative mechanism to complete their studies without any interruption.

Thank you, Chairman, Sir.

Title:  Regarding transfer of khalasies working in FCI. 

SHRI SAPTAGIRI SANKAR ULAKA (KORAPUT): Sir, thank you for giving me this opportunity to raise a matter of urgent public importance relating to my constituency Koraput during the `Zero Hour’. 

Around 113 khalasies are engaged in two FCI/FSD depots of Umeri, Jeypore and Rayagada for the last 30 years on as daily wagers. Now, FCI has unilaterally taken a decision to transfer these people to a faraway place, namely Balijoree in Jharsuguda district, which is around 650 kilometres from the present location. They are all Adivasis and women. 

They are poor people and have been working in these depots and living in the undivided Koraput district for the last 30 years and now if they are transferred to such a distant place, how will these people sustain their livelihood? They are not getting their allowances and have filed a Writ Petition in the High Court of Odisha. Title:  Request to declare wild boar as vermin in Kerala. 

SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN (KASARAGOD): Wild boar is classed as least concern for wildlife protection by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and it has become an invasive species posing threat to crops and human life in part of its introduced ranges.

In Kerala, wild boar has turned into a menace for the farmers as the animal has been causing widespread crop loss in the State. Recently, wild boar attacks claimed several lives in my constituency, Kasaragod. The Government of Kerala has approached the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, for classifying wild boar as vermin. If wild boar is declared vermin under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, it can be culled. Since the Act is a Central Act, only the Union Government can modify it and reclassify the animals.

The Central Government may by notification, declare any wild animal, other than those specified in Schedule I and Part 11 of Schedule H of the Act, to be vermin for any area for a given period of time. As long as the notification is in force, such wild animal shall be included in Schedule V of the Act, depriving them of any protection under the Act. Wild boar is classed as least concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and it has turned into a menace for the farmers in Kerala, especially in my constituency, Kasaragod.

So, I urge upon the Union Government to declare wild boar as vermin in Kerala. Thank you very much, Sir.

Title:  Request to provide suitable help to the medical students in any possible form for the hands-on training in authorized hospitals of respective states. 

श्री हिबी ईडन (एरनाकुलम) : माननीय सभापति महोदय, आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद  । मेरा विषय बहुत ही महत्वपूर्ण है, इसलिए आपसे दो मिनट अधिक मांग रहा हूँ  । 

Sir, there is a huge uncertainty and concern amongst the students and their parents who are pursuing the medical education. Especially after the COVID pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war, the situation has been very pathetic. More than 90 per cent of students have taken heavy educational loans and their future is uncertain. The COVID-19 induced pandemic has destabilized the practices in the education sector. With the new normal changing the practices and norms of the education sector, there has been a major shift in the medium of teaching. The shift to online classes has been greatly lauded and has benefitted many students to continue their education. While these online classes serve their purpose of teaching theory subjects, the students that have enrolled for degrees such as Medicine and other Science courses are being deprived of practical classes which are vital for their practice. For the last two years, foreign medical students enrolled in universities, especially in China and Ukraine and Phillipines etc., have been going through a tough time with mounting mental stress, worrying about uncertainties in completing their degree course. Most of them are on the verge of committing suicide with the current travel restrictions in place. 

As per a reply from the Directorate of Health Services, Kerala, assistance in clinical training can be provided with appropriate permission from host universities, which the students have obtained. Therefore, I request the Union Government and the State Government to look into the matter, so that suitable help can be provided to the students in any possible form for the hands-on training in authorized hospitals of respective States.

Title:  Regarding to consider revising wages paid under the MGNREGS Scheme.

Title:  Request to reform the roof top Solar programme to increase the share of residential sector in the total solar power capacity. 

SHRI KURUVA GORANTLA MADHAV (HINDUPUR): India has committed towards net-zero emissions by 2070 and achieving non-fossil fuel energy capacity of 500 GW by 2030. The Government's push for utility-scale projects is appreciated. However, the rooftop solar programme in the country has failed to pick-up. In this regard, I would like to request the Government of India to do easy financing and unrestricted net metering, and keep an easy regulatory process which could really spur up the growth of the sector. Public financial institutions and other key lenders could also be mandated to lend to the sector. Thus, I would request the Minister of New and Renewable Energy to simplify the process and reform the rooftop solar programme to increase the share of residential sector in the total solar power capacity.
